The company started in 1995, as a spinoff (IPO) of the chemical operations of Sandoz, which then merged its pharmaceutical business with that of Ciba-Geigy to form Novartis.

Clariant AG is a Swiss multinational speciality chemicals company, formed in 1995 as a spin-off from Sandoz. Headquartered in Muttenz, Switzerland the public company encompasses 74 subsidiaries in 36 countries (2022). Major manufacturing sites are located in Europe, North America, South America, China, and India. In 2022, sales from continuing operations were 5.198 billion CHF.

In 1997, Clariant grew substantially, with the acquisition of the Hoechst speciality chemicals business.

This document details the operating model for Rapid Response to meet the business needs defined by Clariant. This document lists user stories and analytics that provide the scope for this release. During the solution's development, this document will be updated with requirement changes and solution design. This document, at technical go live, shall provide both the requirements and solution. This document does not include test results.

The blueprint sets out the processes and associated functional and technical requirements for configuring the future RapidResponse solution.

The aims of the blueprint are threefold:

Set the baseline for the future-state process for the subsequent deployment project –. Business team and key stakeholders are provided the opportunity to set the direction and establish the future concurrent planning process and resulting new ways of working.

Starting from a predefined Process Framework, the future planning processes are modeled at sufficient level of detail, without detailing out the planner tasks, to reflect the future ways of working of our customers.

Ensure a common understanding of solution scope for each project phase - in terms of functional enablement, the business requirements and resulting capabilities to be configured in RapidResponse are expressed through user stories and accordingly support the detailed deployment planning by the implementation team.

A User Story baseline list of confirmed and sized user stories summarizing future solution requirements is produced and frozen as part of each blueprint exercise.

Optimize available capabilities in RapidResponse and address potential solution gaps - Throughout the series of blueprinting workshop, the team jointly develops a common understanding of the solution enablement approach and areas where the ‘out of the box’ solution does not support the requirements. This allows gaps to be filled in the detailed design stage.

Design principles and solution gaps identified by the project team are discussed, laid out as options and documented as out of scope, if necessary.

The goal throughout the blueprint process is larger than just delivering a document for signoff.

In addition to the deliverables specified in the table of content, the project team builds critical expertise to support the future business transformation enabled by Kinaxis RapidResponse and documents relevant opportunities and risks:

Business Case realization – It is of critical importance during the customer blueprint to ensure we fully acknowledge the ROI expectations from the future project, and clarify how the process changes and new solution enablement will eliminate current painpoints and help materialize the defined business case. A baseline for the critical KPI and the definition of improvement targets is a critical step during a customer blueprint.

Kinaxis Agile Implementation Methodology (AIM) – The customer blueprint is a critical stepping stone supporting the Kinaxis Agile Implementation Methodology. It provides the foundation for both the customer and the Kinaxis implementation team to develop a team spirit and a common project philosophy in preparation of the sprint-based implementations. Agile means different things to different people and alignment on ground principles takes some time.

Concurrent Planning Capabilities – Starting from an overview of the potential capabilities to transform planning in a company, various capabilities and functionalities (Business Dashboards, Scenarios, Analytics, etc.) are covered at various detail levels during the workshop and educational sessions to bring to life the significant improvement opportunities and benefits of concurrent planning.

Data and integration risks – Blueprint workshops help the technical experts on both sides gage the potential data health challenges that could become risks for the future implementation. A complementary data health assessment is a way to fully visualize these risks and anticipate any future issues.

Organizational and change management – At best the project team will also familiarize with the importance of clarifying the new planning roles, establishing clear learning objectives for the various stakeholders, and learn more about the importance of establishing a Kinaxis Center of Excellence to enable and deploy the new ways of working, and continuously learn about the best approach to introduce concurrent planning in the organization.

The importance of the Customer blueprint activity to enable concurrent planning cannot be underestimated. By selecting Kinaxis RapidResponse, a customer is redefining their planning approach, moving away from a static and silo-ed step-by-step process towards an agile, real-time integrated approach based on business dashboards and scenarios.

End-to-End visibility of operations; which requires real-time integration and alignment between all the planning functions around agreed performance KPIs, but also one seamless supply chain network view and planning process connecting all required systems and data across the multiple organizations.

Agile decision-making through a dramatically improved planning frequency, giving all planners and stakeholders near-real time visibility to alerts and risks and access to scenarios and support for immediate and high-quality decisions.

The following section gives an overview of the functional requirements of demand planning in the initial phase of the project:

The Demand Planning process provides Demand Planners with capabilities to manage product lifecycle, input and manage forecasts that contribute to the consensus demand plan, and generate the consensus forecast.

Start with the Historical data as an input.

Normalize the historical data for data errors, outliers, and causals.

Once the history is corrected for errors, If there is a need for any adjustments to the planning BOMs will be performed for the components.

Run the statistical forecast based on the best fit model to create the base forecast.

Apply any known events, promotions activities.

With this as a base demand planners can collaborate with other stakeholders.

Additional adjustments to be made to the plan based on the collaboration with sales, finance teams and various demand drivers that impact the future.

Output of all the above activities reflect the best view of what we could sell. This plan will be discussed in the demand review meeting with the consensus from the supply team for any supplier constraints or logistic issues, final demand plan is generated, and this will be available as active forecast.

New Product Forecasting

When forecasting for a new product, there are three potential streams:

Brand new

No reference SKU available

Requires manual forecast or history build.

New – reference

Reference SKU available, where the history is from One or More SKU ‘copied.’

Both SKUs are forecasted in parallel

New – replace.

Reference SKU available, where the history is ‘copied.’

Supersession model, where the old SKU can still be consumed until inventory is depleted, at which point the new SKU is used as per Profile Setting.
